newsitem.title: GERMANY: German official criticises Russia over war booty.
newsitem.headline: German official criticises Russia over war booty.

text.p: German political spokesmen criticised Russia's Duma on Friday for claiming ownership of art treasures seized from Nazi Germany and looked to the upper house of parliament to quash the move.
Karl-Heinz Hornhues, chairman of the German parliament's foreign policy committee, said in a statement that the Duma was using the issue to attack President Boris Yeltsin.
The bill claiming as Russian property artefacts and works of art seized from the Nazis at the end of World War Two caused outrage in Germany and was vetoed by Yeltsin on March 18.
Russia's communist-dominated lower house of parliament voted 308-15 on Friday to override the veto.

"If the Russian parliament, contrary to all agreements, declares the works of art to be Russian property, it doesn't exactly support the German government's international efforts to present Russia as a reliable partner and friend for the West...," Hornhues said.
"The Russian parliament is obviously using this sensitive topic in German-Russian relations as a stick to beat Yeltsin with," Hornhues said.
Political leaders in Germany have been lobbying hard since the end of the Cold War for the return of the artworks. Bonn said it may raise the subject with Yeltsin when he visits Germany on April 17.
Government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told a news conference Bonn was now looking to the Russian Federation Council (upper house), where a two-thirds majority is also needed to overturn the veto.
"Whether this issue has effects (on the relationship between Russia and Germany), well I wouldn't put it like that," he said.

If the Council, which also heavily supported the original bill, does override the veto, Yeltsin will have to sign the law, making all art treasures brought to the Soviet Union as a result of World War Two the inalienable property of the Russian state.
The Kremlin may, however, ask Russia's Constitutional Court to look into the matter.
